cues.text: Thank you for joining me for this brief
tutorial focused on managing pipette
calibration plans for use with the MVS
in the ArtelWare software application.
We've got a lot of ground to cover. So,
let's go ahead and get started.
Your MVS pipette calibration plan is where
you'll define how many replicates that
you're going to take for each pipette
calibration, what volumes and what
tolerance limits are going to be applied
to each of those volumes when you
perform your pipette calibrations. There
are a couple of different ways to add a
calibration plan to the ArtelWare
software. The first way is to click on
the create plan shortcut on the get
started bar. The second way is to
navigate to the configuration section of
the left side navigation panel and then
go to the calibration plans section.
Let's go ahead and go back to the home
screen and let's use the create plan
shortcut on the get started bar. We're
going to select pipette calibration and
we'll click okay. Your pipette calibration
plan name typically contains information
about the volume of the pipette that
you're testing as well as whether or not
it's a fixed volume pipette or an
adjustable or variable volume pipette.
For today, we are going to be creating a
calibration plan for 100 microL
multi-channel pipette. The description
field is optional, so we'll leave that
blank. but information such as a
specific volume that you might be
testing with this calibration plan, that
information could go here. The next
thing that you'll want to select is your
measurement type. Because we're going to
be using the Artl MVS, we want to make
sure that we've selected the Artel MBS
for our measurement type. Next, we'll
determine the plate type. And in this
case, I only have 96 well as an option
because I do not have the 384 well plate
support added into my software. If
you're interested in a 384 well support
add-on, please contact your account
manager.
Next, we'll determine the number of
channels that are in the device. In this
particular case, this is an 8 channel
pipette.
Then, we'll determine what type of
orientation that we'd like to use.
Because this is an 8 channel pipette,
there's only one orientation that's
available, and that's vertical. If I was
using a 4 channel pipette,
then I'd have some options. But I'm
using an eight channel pipette
and tip spacing will remain as
contigious wells. I don't have any other
options. I can't alternate wells with
this eight channel device in a vertical
orientation.
Next, I'll need to take a look at the
tolerances and determine what types of
tolerances that I want to use with this
pipette calibration. I have a few
different options. I can use the pipette
manufacturer specification or I can use
the ISO 86552022
permissible tolerances table or the
ISO8655
2002 permissible tolerances table or I
can define my own tolerances based on
user requirements. I'm going to go ahead
and select userdefined.
Next, I need to make some decisions
about how I would like to see my data. I
can choose to include channel statistics
in my evaluation criteria, as well as
dispense order statistics in my
evaluation criteria. If I'm interested
in seeing these, but I don't want my
evaluation criteria to be pass or failed
based on these, I can certainly uncheck
these boxes.
Let's go ahead and include the channel
statistics because I'm testing an eight
channel pipette and that's important to
me. Next, I'll go to the dispense step
section because this is where I'll
define what wells are being tested, what
volumes are being tested, and what the
pass or fill tolerances are for each
volume. To add a dispense step, click on
the plus sign for create new dispense
step. Next, I'll define my dispense
volume.
So I'm running a quick check on this
particular pipe head. So I'm going to
select 10 microL
with four replicates per channel and I'm
going to assign my inaccuracy and
imprecision tolerances.
Next I need to select a color that will
represent the wells within this plate
and I'll select add dispense step. Our
tell will show you a brief tutorial on
how to do this. If you don't want to see
that tutorial again, you can check the
box for do not show this message again.
I'm going to go ahead and click okay.
Then I'm going to select the wells where
I want these 10 microL dispenses to be
dispensed into. Now I'm performing a
routine check with this variable volume
pipe head. And I don't want to test just
at its low end. I want to test its mid
and high ends as well. So I'm going to
go ahead and click on this plus sign to
add another dispense step where I'm
testing at 50 microL.
I'll select four replicates again. Then
I'll enter my tolerances for inaccuracy
and imprecision for this 50 microL test.
I'll go ahead and I'll select a
different color to represent the
dispensing of the wells.
And I'll select the wells that I want
these 50 microL replicates to be
dispensed into.
Last to complete this routine test I'll
add one last volume which is at 100
microL the highest volume in this
pipette four replicates and once again
entering my inaccuracy and imprecision
specification
and this time I'll select another color
to represent my wells and I'll go ahead
and map my plate.
I can add additional plates and
additional dispense steps, but because
this is a routine test, I'm going to go
ahead and leave it as is. I'll go ahead
and select approved. And if there's an
additional review comment that you want
to add, you can certainly do that here
or accept the default one. I'm going to
accept the default
and click okay.
And now you can see that my 100 microL
variable multi-channel pipette calibration
plan is now listed.
There are a couple of other icons that
are on this screen that might be of
interest. So once your calibration plan
list grows a bit larger, you may choose
to filter so that you can quickly locate
various calibration plans. There's a
refresh icon on this screen. There is
also an import MVS data manager plate
layout in this screen. If you have MVS
Data Manager versions 3.6 or 3.7, you
can export those plate layouts and
import them into our Telware. There's
also a clone selected calibration plan
icon. So, if you want to clone this
calibration plan, but maybe you want to
call it a different name, you could
certainly do that.
Or if you want to create another
calibration plan from this screen,
simply click on the plus sign.
Now, you'll notice that the calibration
version is version one for this
multi-channel calibration plan I just
created. In your RTLWware verification
reports, it will include the list of the
calibration plan name that was used as
well as the version. If I want to edit
this particular calibration plan, I can
click on the edit icon and then you'll
notice that my version immediately
versions to version two and it will
continue to version. for each edit that
I make.
A couple of other useful pieces of
information that you might find in this
calibration plan screen is an icon to
view schedules that that calibration
plan might be included in. Or if you
wanted to deactivate your selected
calibration plan, you could do that as
well. So, a special thing to note is
that if your calibration plan is linked
to a schedule, you will have to remove
the calibration plan from your schedule
prior to deactivating it. And once you
deactivate a calibration plan, you
cannot reactivate that calibration plan.
So that's important to note as well.
Okay, that concludes our brief tutorial.
Do you have additional questions? Please
contact us at 1 800225434
option3 or at supporticmp.com.
Thank you.
